note: Braids' SAW_COMB has exactly two axes. TIMBRE is parameter_[0] and it is the COMB PITCH: digital_oscillator.cc:248 reads `pitch_ + ((parameter_[0] - 16384) >> 1)`, i.e. -64..+64 semitones about the played note, so it maps to the engine's TIMBRE. COLOR is parameter_[1] and it is the FEEDBACK: digital_oscillator.cc:261-263 forms `(parameter_[1] << 1) - 32768` and warps it through ws_moderate_overdrive, so it is bipolar and it maps to the engine's HARMONICS. MACRO sits at 0.5 in every case -- ApplyMacro(0.0, 0.6, -0.6, macro) returns tilt 0 at noon, which is Braids' flat loop. MORPH sits at 0.0, NOT at noon: saw_comb_engine.cc sets waveshape = 0.5 + 0.5*morph and pw = 0.5 - 0.25*morph, and VariableShapeOscillator is a plain saw at waveshape 0.5 with pw 0.5, so MORPH 0 is the AnalogOscillator OSC_SHAPE_SAW exciter of macro_oscillator.cc:366-369 while MORPH 0.5 is a half-square at 37.5% duty, which the module cannot make. SPEC R11 allows this (MORPH has no detent), but it does mean noon is not stock on this engine. The morph-noon-not-stock case at the end exists only to pin that number; it is deliberately off-axis and is not a fidelity claim.
auditNote: CORRECTNESS PASS 2026-07-29. An earlier audit DECLARED four deviations and deliberately left the DSP alone; this pass FIXED them, and every tolerance below was re-derived from what the engine now achieves. What changed in the engine -- all of it reproducing quantised Braids arithmetic that a closed form had smoothed away, which is this campaign's recurring defect class: (1) the comb-pitch smoother is now Braids' integer recursion `(15 * filtered_pitch + pitch) >> 4` in 1/128-semitone units, whose floor makes every value in [p-15, p] a fixed point, so rising from the 0 Init() memsets it STALLS 15 LSB = 11.72 cents FLAT of its target -- verified at exactly -15 LSB for every case pitch in this file, where the port's float pole converged exactly and so ran 11.72 cents sharp for the life of every note; (2) the comb pitch now carries ComputeDelay's ceiling of kHighestNote - kOctave = 16384 = MIDI 128 (digital_oscillator.cc:73-76), which the port had no equivalent of; (3) the feedback warp is now ws_moderate_overdrive's own generator rather than a normalised SoftLimit, so the maximum feedback is the module's truncated 32728/32768 = 0.998779 and the loop DECAYS, where the port's was exactly 1.0 and marginally stable; (4) the output clipper is hard, as `CLIP(out)` (digital_oscillator.cc:278) is, not SoftClip; (5) a trigger no longer resets anything, because Braids' SAW_COMB is inert under a strike -- MacroOscillator::Strike reaches DigitalOscillator::Strike, which only sets strike_, and RenderComb never reads it -- and the smoother is seeded to Braids' own 0 rather than a fixed MIDI 48. Seven cases were ADDED to cover regimes nothing here reached: the three unvisited corners of the two-axis space, the comb-pitch ceiling both 16 LSB UNDER its knee and 19 semitones PAST it, a TIMBRE sweep that crosses it, and a second triggered case at a note BELOW the old fixed seed. Every added case moves materially between the old engine and this one -- corner-low-high 4.43 -> 0.48 dB, comb-ceiling-deep 3.30 -> 0.80 dB, trigger-low 1.82 -> 0.20 dB -- so none of them is decoration. VERIFICATION PASS, same day: a SIXTH clamp was found missing and fixed. Braids clamps its own pitch_ to [0, kHighestNote] in DigitalOscillator::Render (digital_oscillator.cc:120-124) BEFORE dispatching to RenderComb, so the note the TIMBRE offset applies to is already pinned at MIDI 0 from below; the port applied the offset to Plaits' raw note, which reaches -119 (voice.cc:265), and so ran its comb up to an octave flat of the module's under a downward pitch CV. The eighth added case, low-note-clamp, covers it: 0.54 -> 0.05 dB. Nothing at or above MIDI 36 moves, so no other case in this file changed by a hundredth of a dB.
tolerances: Tolerances are set to what the engine NOW achieves, with roughly 1.4x headroom on the small numbers. Exactly ONE number in this file is looser than it was before the correctness pass: morph-noon-not-stock's acRmsDb, 1.0 -> 2.5. That case is the deliberately off-axis MORPH diagnostic, it is not a fidelity claim, and its level grew because the port stopped soft-clipping -- SoftClip had been pulling 1.25 dB off everything, so +2.21 dB is the honest size of the half-square-vs-saw difference and +0.76 dB was the understated one. Every other tolerance in the file was TIGHTENED. Twenty-one of the twenty-three cases sit under 1.2 dB spectrum and under 0.6 dB AC RMS, inside the guide's ~1 dB / ~1 cent / ~1.5 dB target; every case carries a cents tolerance, including the two that could not before, and every one of those is inside 0.5 cents except low-note-clamp, whose 5.2 is a documented estimator artefact rather than a pitch error (see its own note). Three sit outside the spectrum target, each for a measured reason. (1) res-inverted, at 2.93 dB, is the deep-cancellation corner: HARMONICS 0 gives g = -32766/32768 = -0.999939, a Q around 16,000, and TIMBRE noon lays the comb's null ladder over the exciter's own harmonics. What the reference outputs there is the RESIDUAL of a >30 dB cancellation -- 26% of its energy sits in 5-10 kHz, which reads -5.4 dB -- and at that null depth a sub-LSB difference in the fractional-delay interpolator is worth several dB of it. Its sibling res-ringing, the same |g| to four places but POSITIVE, so the peaks land on the harmonics rather than the nulls, reads 0.24 dB in this same file: that is the evidence this is null-residual sensitivity and not a feedback-path error. (2) res-low-detuned at 1.16 dB is the same effect an order of magnitude weaker (g = -0.918, Q around 12). (3) morph-noon-not-stock is deliberately off-axis and is not a fidelity claim; see its own note. TESTED AND REJECTED as an explanation for res-inverted: tuning the comb delay to absolute 48 kHz instead of to Plaits' kCorrectedSampleRate, which would put the comb at Braids' exact Hz but 4.61 cents out of tune with the port's OWN note. That made everything worse -- stock 0.40 -> 1.53 dB, comb-low-open 0.45 -> 2.86 dB, res-inverted 2.93 -> 3.76 dB -- confirming that the comb's tuning relative to the note, which both sides get exactly right, is what governs these cases, and that the global 4.61-cent transposition the port shares with every other ported engine is not the residual here.

cases.name: TIMBRE noon, HARMONICS noon
cases.why: The comb sits on the played note and the feedback is ~0, so this is the pure FIR comb the README describes: 0.5*dry plus one echo, audible, not silent. It is the case the comb-pitch quantiser hurt most -- the module's 11.72-cent stall puts a ~33 dB null on the 70th harmonic, 7.7 kHz here, and the port's exactly-converged pole put no null anywhere, worth +10.18 dB in 5-10 kHz. Now that the port stalls with it that band reads -0.62 dB and the case is 0.40. AC RMS went -1.25 -> -0.01 dB when the output clipper stopped being SoftClip.

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 at note 45 -- delay clamped
cases.why: Bottom of the TIMBRE axis. comb_note = 45 - 64 = -19, below the MIDI -16 at which Braids' ComputeDelay shifts by a NEGATIVE count and returns 0 -- which its own `delay_ptr + 2*kCombDelayLength - 0` then reads as a full-line 8,192-tap delay. The port clamps to its own full line, 4,096 taps at 48 kHz, the same 85.33 ms; that clamp was widened from 4,094 in this pass so the two land on the same delay rather than two taps apart. This is the case that proves the README's 'clamps below MIDI ~70 just as it does on hardware' claim.

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 at note 84 -- delay NOT clamped
cases.why: The same TIMBRE end, above the MIDI ~70 knee, so the delay is live rather than clamped: comb_note = 19.875 = 25.8 Hz, about 1,857 taps at 48 kHz. This was the clearest read on the comb-pitch quantiser -- 11.72 cents on a 1,857-tap delay is a 12.6-tap offset, which put the two null ladders half a null out of step from ~1.3 kHz upward and left an alternating +4.49 / -6.25 dB band pattern at 3.57 dB overall. Reproducing the stall takes it to 0.45 dB, with every band carrying real energy inside 1.19 dB.

cases.name: TIMBRE 1 at note 45
cases.why: Top of the TIMBRE axis at a played note LOW enough that the comb-pitch ceiling does not engage: comb_note = 108.875, an ~10.9-tap delay at 4.4 kHz. Together with comb-lowest this pins the direction and the full +-64 semitone span; a sign error or a halved range would put this case tens of dB out rather than under 1 dB. The ceiling itself is covered by comb-ceiling-knee and comb-ceiling-deep.

cases.name: TIMBRE 1 at note 84 -- past the module's comb-pitch ceiling
cases.why: comb_note = 84 + 64 = 148, which Braids' ComputeDelay pins at kHighestNote - kOctave = 16384 = MIDI 128 = 13.29 kHz (digital_oscillator.cc:73-76). The port had no such ceiling and put its comb at 21.15 kHz, nearly an octave up: 10.24-20.48 kHz read -8.18 dB while carrying 19.1% of the reference's energy, and the case sat at 2.22 dB. With the ceiling reproduced it is 0.49 dB and that band reads -2.07 dB.

cases.name: The same ceiling with the comb resonant
cases.why: The same ceiling with HARMONICS at 0.9, so the comb has a resonant PEAK rather than shallow nulls -- which is what made the size of the old deviation unmissable: 4.27 dB, with 10.24-20.48 kHz at -13.19 dB carrying 21.7% of the reference's energy, i.e. roughly 30% of the module's output sitting in a resonance the port did not have. Now 0.86 dB. It also carries a cents tolerance for the first time: with both combs pinned at 13.29 kHz the autocorrelation estimator locks the 1046 Hz saw fundamental on both sides, where before the port's 21 kHz ring defeated it.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0 -- full negative feedback
cases.why: Bottom of the COLOR axis, and the loosest case in the file at 2.93 dB. It proves the feedback is genuinely BIPOLAR: `(parameter_[1] << 1) - 32768` is -32768 here, the table returns -32766, and the loop inverts. It is loose because it is the deep-cancellation corner -- see the file's tolerances note. |g| = 0.999939 gives a Q around 16,000 and TIMBRE noon lays the comb's null ladder over the exciter's own harmonics, so what the reference outputs is the residual of a >30 dB cancellation and a sub-LSB difference in the fractional-delay interpolator is worth several dB of it. res-ringing, the same |g| to four places but positive, reads 0.24 dB. The fix still moved this case from 3.76 to 2.93 dB and its level from -2.53 to -1.26 dB.

cases.name: HARMONICS 1 -- full positive feedback
cases.why: Top of the COLOR axis, and the case that pins the feedback CEILING. `resonance` is 32766 only BEFORE the warp; Interpolate88 then reads ws_moderate_overdrive at index 65534, and that table's last two entries are both 32728, because its generator sets x[-1] = x[-2] before scaling. So the module's maximum feedback is 32728/32768 = 0.998779 and its loop DECAYS. A normalised SoftLimit reached exactly 1.0 and did not: the port's ring built to an equilibrium set only by its in-loop clip, which put both bands above 2.5 kHz at +14 dB and the case at 2.42 dB. Reproducing the generator takes it to 0.24 dB with no band past 1.5 dB.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0.85 with the comb detuned up
cases.why: Strongly resonant but short of the unity corner, and off the TIMBRE detent, so it exercises both axes together in the region a player actually uses. 1.06 -> 0.27 dB.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0.15 with the comb detuned down
cases.why: The negative-but-not-extreme quadrant, on the other side of noon from res-high and at a different note, so a swap of the two Braids parameters cannot survive this case together with res-high. At 1.16 dB it is the second-loosest case, for a weaker version of res-inverted's reason: g = -0.918 still puts nulls rather than peaks against the drive, at a Q around 12 rather than 16,000. The residual is in the two top bands (5-10 kHz -2.25 dB, 10-20 kHz -4.37 dB, 29% of the energy between them); everything from 160 Hz to 5 kHz is inside 0.4 dB.

cases.name: TIMBRE swept 0 to 1
cases.why: The whole comb-pitch axis in one render, which averages the per-null disagreement away and so measures the axis MAPPING rather than its fine structure. An inverted or rescaled TIMBRE would not average out. It also exercises the smoother IN MOTION rather than at its stall -- a sweep never settles -- so it is the case that would catch the integer recursion being run at the wrong block rate.

cases.name: TIMBRE swept 0 to 1 through the ceiling
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29. The same sweep two octaves up, so it CROSSES the comb-pitch ceiling partway: comb_note reaches MIDI 128 at TIMBRE 0.844 and is pinned from there to the top. Nothing else in the file exercises the ceiling engaging while the smoother is still moving, which is the one place a disagreement between the ceiling and the smoother would show as a glitch rather than as a steady offset.

cases.name: Comb 16 LSB under the ceiling
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29. The BOUNDARY of the comb-pitch ceiling from below: note 96 with parameter_[0] = 24575 gives a target of 16383 and a stalled pitch of 16368, sixteen LSB under the 16384 the ceiling pins to. The ceiling must NOT engage here. Paired with comb-ceiling-deep this is what distinguishes a correct ceiling from one placed an octave, a semitone or a single LSB wrong -- a clamp tested only far past its knee cannot tell those apart.

cases.name: Comb 19 semitones past the ceiling
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29. The other side of that boundary, and the deepest excursion past it in the file: the requested comb pitch is MIDI 147.2 and the module pins it at 128. The unclamped port read 3.30 dB here; it now reads 0.80. Note 96 is also the highest played note in the file, so this doubles as the top of the note range.

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 with HARMONICS 0
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29. The file covered each axis at both ends but never the two ends TOGETHER, so a bug that only shows when both are extreme had nowhere to appear. Note 84 keeps the comb off its bottom clamp and the delay live: comb_note = 19.875, about 1,857 taps, running at |g| = 0.999939. 1.79 -> 0.67 dB.

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 with HARMONICS 1
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29, and the single largest mover of the seven added cases: 4.43 -> 0.48 dB. A long, live 1,857-tap delay at the feedback ceiling is where the difference between a loop that decays at 0.998779 and one sitting at exactly 1.0 compounds hardest, because it combines the most round trips per second with the least loss per round trip.

cases.name: TIMBRE 1 with HARMONICS 1
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29. The last unvisited corner: an ~4.6-tap comb at 10.5 kHz ringing at the feedback ceiling. comb_note = 123.875 sits just under the MIDI 128 ceiling, so this tests the top of TIMBRE WITHOUT the clamp; the clamped version of the same corner is comb-clamp-highest-res.

cases.name: HARMONICS swept 0 to 1
cases.why: The whole feedback axis, inverted through FIR comb to ringing, in one render. It used to read 1.54 dB with the two sub-80 Hz bands at -22 to -24 dB -- the subsonic wander a comb with positive feedback and no DC blocker parks in its line, bounded on each side only by its own clipper, and the two clippers differed. With both clippers hard it is 0.39 dB and those bands are inside 0.15 dB.

cases.name: Both axes mid, two octaves up
cases.why: comb_note = 103.078, an ~15-tap delay ringing at ~3.2 kHz against a 1046 Hz saw. This case used to carry NO cents tolerance: the strongest periodicity in the port's output was inharmonic with the note, and ab_compare's autocorrelation locked the reference to 1046.0 Hz and the port to 262.3 Hz -- a 2399-cent octave-quadrupling artefact of the estimator. Both sides now read inside 0.2 cents and it carries a real tolerance, because the port's comb is where the module's is.

cases.name: Repeated triggers -- the module is inert under a strike
cases.why: Braids' SAW_COMB is the right control for a trigger case, because it does NOTHING: MacroOscillator::Strike reaches DigitalOscillator::Strike, which only sets strike_, and RenderComb never reads it. So any difference here was the port's alone -- and there was one. READ THE BANDS: the old headline was 0.48 dB only because the affected bands carried 0.0% of the reference's energy, while `--bands` showed 20-40 Hz +22.40 dB, 40-80 Hz +25.70 dB and 320-640 Hz +23.72 dB against a module with essentially nothing there. That was the port's per-note Reset() -- the delay-line clear, the exciter phase reset, and above all `comb_pitch_ = 48.0f`, which at note 84 forced a 36-semitone comb glide at the start of every note. The trigger reset is gone; those three bands now read -6.97, -9.37 and -8.02 dB, i.e. the port is if anything QUIETER than the module in bands where neither has anything, and the case is 0.39.

cases.name: Repeated triggers below the old fixed seed
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29, and the tightest case in the file at 0.20 dB. trigger-transient sits ABOVE the old MIDI 48 seed, so its per-note glide ran upward; this one sits twelve semitones BELOW it, so the same bug glided DOWNWARD, and at a resonance high enough (HARMONICS 0.7) for the glide to ring rather than pass. On the old engine it read 1.82 dB and -1.45 dB AC RMS. A future reinstatement of a per-trigger reset, in EITHER direction, fails here first.

cases.name: Played note below MIDI 0, comb at the top of TIMBRE
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29 BY THE VERIFICATION PASS, because nothing in this file went below MIDI 36 and the note the comb offsets from is CLAMPED on the module. DigitalOscillator::Render pins its own pitch_ to [0, kHighestNote] before dispatching to RenderComb (digital_oscillator.cc:120-124), so at note -12 with TIMBRE 1 the module's comb sits at 0 + 8191 = MIDI 63.99 while an unclamped port put it at -1536 + 8191 = MIDI 51.99 -- an octave flat. Plaits' note reaches -119 (voice.cc:265), so this is reachable with any downward pitch CV. On the engine as the correctness pass left it this read 0.54 dB with 160-320 Hz at +6.09 dB, the port's misplaced comb resonance; with the clamp reproduced it is 0.05 dB and no band is past 0.1 dB except the shared HF exciter deficit. THE 5.2-CENT TOLERANCE IS AN ESTIMATOR ARTEFACT, NOT A PITCH ERROR: below about MIDI 24 the fundamental is under 9 Hz, ab_compare's autocorrelation has no resolvable fundamental and locks onto the comb period instead, where its lag resolution is coarser than the 4.61-cent kCorrectedSampleRate transposition it is correcting for -- so both sides read the same raw lag and the corrected figure shows the full -4.6. Verified as an artefact by rendering the same settings at notes 0, 12 and 24, where the clamp does nothing and the reading is still -4.6.

cases.name: DIAGNOSTIC: MORPH at noon is not the module
cases.why: DELIBERATELY OFF-AXIS -- not a fidelity claim but a pinned number, and its are the only loose tolerances in the file that do not describe a defect. Identical to the stock case except MORPH is at noon, which gives waveshape 0.75 and pw 0.375: a half-square exciter at 37.5% duty, not the module's saw. The +2.21 dB AC RMS is the honest size of that difference now that the port no longer soft-clips its output; the old +0.76 dB understated it, because SoftClip was quietly pulling 1.25 dB off everything. Kept so the claim stays re-runnable with one command.
